title: Interpersonal Theory of Mind Processing Pipeline
objective: Process bounded human-interaction text into an evidence-bounded external-state, internal-hypothesis, and recursive-epistemic analysis without converting inference into fact.

deterministicSemantics.rule: Deterministic structure does not imply objective access to private mental states.

epistemicLevels.label: L1
epistemicLevels.definition: What Actor A appears to believe, want, fear, know, or intend.

epistemicLevels.label: L2
epistemicLevels.definition: What Actor A appears to believe Actor B believes, wants, fears, knows, or intends.

epistemicLevels.label: L3
epistemicLevels.definition: What Actor A appears to want Actor B to believe about Actor A's own belief, intention, knowledge, or stance.

frameworks.name: Dennett's Intentional Stance
frameworks.use: Model an actor as operating from beliefs, desires, information, incentives, constraints, and internal logic.
frameworks.guardrail: Explanatory stance only; do not treat inferred beliefs/desires as established private facts or assume perfect rationality.

frameworks.name: Fonagy Mentalization Model
frameworks.use: Assess evidence of successful or failed attempts to represent another person's mental state.
frameworks.guardrail: Use observed mentalization quality / possible failure language; do not make a clinical diagnosis.

frameworks.name: Rogers Congruence
frameworks.use: Compare observed external presentation with the best-supported hypothesized internal operational state.
frameworks.guardrail: Ordinal evidence-bounded assessment unless a separate quantitative scoring model has been explicitly defined.

heuristics.label: Concrete vs. Abstract Rumination
heuristics.positiveDefinition: Concrete processing stays specific, testable, bounded, actionable, and revisable.
heuristics.flagDefinition: Abstract rumination globalizes into difficult-to-test questions about character, intent, permanent defect, destiny, or meaning without producing new evidence or action.

heuristics.label: Manufactured Obligation
heuristics.flagDefinition: Unsolicited, substitutionary, exaggerated, or strategically reframed help is used to generate unearned guilt, gratitude, debt, or compliance.

heuristics.label: Totalitarian Guardrails
heuristics.flagDefinition: Absolute conversational rules function to preclude contrary evidence, redefine disagreement as disloyalty/pathology, or immunize a fixed narrative from revision.
exclusions: procedural constraints unless used to suppress relevant divergent evidence

heuristics.label: Imposter Morality / Sociopathic Self-Image
heuristics.flagDefinition: The subject's own words or strongly contextualized behavior support a self-image in which positive traits, empathy, generosity, or morality are interpreted as calculated performance masking an inherently malicious or defective self.
heuristics.guardrail: Self-image pattern only; never diagnose sociopathy, psychopathy, ASPD, or another mental-health condition.

passes.title: External State Isolation
passes.prohibition: Do not infer motive in this pass.

passes.title: Internal State Approximation
passes.rule: Generate evidence-bounded hypotheses only after the external evidence ledger exists.

passes.title: Epistemic Layering
passes.rule: Track only recursive levels supported by the text, up to depth 3.

sections.title: Recursive Mind-Map (Epistemic Chain)
sections.format: Indented hierarchy using L1/L2/L3 where supported.

sections.title: Structural Blind Spots & Reasoning Flaws
sections.format: Bulleted index with evidence basis or explicit insufficient-evidence statement.

heuristicFamily.label: TheraminTrees-inspired modalities
heuristicFamily.guardrail: Do not treat these labels as validated psychiatric constructs, diagnoses, or automatic moral verdicts.

decisionPressureAndMoralContext.tragicDecisionStructure: Flag when every option reasonably perceived by the actor carried serious cost. This does not imply equal moral quality across options.
governingRules: Behavior under coercion or severe constraint is not equivalent to agreement.

minimalRecursionRule: Use the lowest recursive depth sufficient to explain the interaction. L2 and L3 each require independent evidence.

continuousStateModel.actorStateFormula: S(t+1) = Update[S(t), stimuli, interaction, environmental change, memory activation, reinforcement, punishment, new information, role change, consequences, self-reflection]
continuousStateModel.actionEmissionFormula: Action(t) = Expression[S(t), situation, role, incentives, audience, capability, coercion, habit, masking]
continuousStateModel.observerModelFormula: M(O→T,t+1) = Revise[M(O→T,t), observed action, known context, prior relationship, source quality, environmental evidence, uncertainty]
principles: Actor state trajectory and observer model trajectory are separate evolving systems.
Action is an emission from internal state under context and constraint, not direct access to private state.
The target may change without the observer updating; the observer may update when the target has not changed.
Previous interpersonal models act as priors on interpretation of new evidence.
Dyadic models must ingest relevant exogenous changes before each new direct interaction.
Event time, knowledge time, and reinterpretation time are distinct.
Multiple observers may rationally update differently from the same action because their priors and context differ.

selfTheoryOfMind.distinction: The actor's self-model is separate from the actor's underlying state trajectory S(A,t).
selfTheoryOfMind.updateFormula: M(A→A,t+1) = ReviseSelf[M(A→A,t), introspection, memory, action, consequence, external feedback, observer reactions, new information, role change, self-reflection]
principles: Self-report is important evidence but not infallible proof of complete causal understanding.
Direct reports of subjective experience may be stronger evidence of felt experience than of the full causal explanation for behavior.
High introspective confidence does not imply high self-model accuracy.
Ordinary self-model error does not require pathology.
Autobiographical memory is part of the self-model and may be reconstructed or reinterpreted.
Other people can provide feedback that changes or challenges an actor's self-model.
Self-predictions should be preserved and tested against later behavior rather than rewritten retrospectively.
Later reinterpretation does not overwrite the actor's earlier self-understanding.
selfTheoryOfMind.selfDeceptionGuardrail: Do not label self-deception merely because the actor is wrong about themselves. Prefer narrower explanations unless evidence shows active maintenance of a belief against information the actor possesses or repeatedly encounters.

realPeople: Do not diagnose from text or public behavior.
Use documented diagnoses or directly attributable evidence only when clinically relevant.
A documented condition does not by itself prove causal responsibility for a specific decision.
Preserve ordinary non-clinical explanations when sufficient.
fictionalCharacters: Use authorially established or canonically evidenced conditions where available.
Do not invent pathology when ordinary incentives, emotion, incomplete information, or character history explain the behavior.

examples: L1: A believes I want X.
L2: A believes I believe I want X because I am the kind of person who values Y.
L3: A believes others think I want X, and I want them to understand my real reason is Y.

normativeSelfGuidance.distinction: Normative self-guidance is separate from the actor's underlying state S(A,t) and descriptive self-model M(A→A,t).
normativeSelfGuidance.actionSelectionGapPrinciple: normative guidance, intention, self-prediction, and actual action may diverge and must be represented separately.
governingRules: A person may accurately know what they believe they should do and still fail to do it.
Internal contradiction is not automatically irrational or pathological.
Later belief that I should have done X does not prove X was available or foreseeable at decision time.
Post-action self-judgment is another model state and may itself be accurate, incomplete, defensive, overly harsh, or distorted.
Target state, target self-model, target normative guidance, observer model, and analyst hypothesis must remain distinct.
normativeSelfGuidance.llmModelingStance: The executing reasoning system does not claim a lived internal theory of mind. It maintains separate evidence-bounded models of targets, including self-models, normative guidance, observer models, temporal transitions, and uncertainty.

relationshipHysteresis.rule: Current evidence is interpreted through accumulated relationship history; restored circumstances do not reset the relationship automatically.

modelLag.rule: Separate target state-change time from observer recognition time.

sharedEpistemicGround.rule: Shared knowledge state is distinct from ordinary recursive belief depth.

signaling.rule: Do not assume signaling intent without evidence or strategic context.

evidenceDiagnosticity.rule: Behavior that is costly, difficult to fake, and consistent with few competing hypotheses is usually more diagnostic than low-cost statements, without becoming automatically truthful or virtuous.

relationshipRepair.rule: Forgiveness, reconciliation, affection, cooperation, and trust recovery are distinct.

valueHierarchy.rule: A value may remain present even when another value overrides it in a particular decision.

outcomeBiasControl.rule: Evaluate decision quality from information and alternatives available at decision time before evaluating outcome.

provenanceDependentUncertainty.rule: Repeated reports derived from one underlying source are not independent confirmation.

metacognitiveCalibration.rule: Accurate uncertainty is preferable to confident unsupported certainty.

memorySalience.rule: Retained memory and actively retrieved, decision-relevant memory are distinct.

institutionalTheoryOfMind.rule: Do not infer that every institution member shares the institution's apparent motive.
